vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.zh:
n. 风琴, 器官, 元件, 机构, 机关

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.zh:

n. a periodical that publishes critical essays on current affairs or literature or art

parts.text: Researchers have also investigated seated “soleus push-ups”: repeated heel raises that work a

deep in the calf. In a 2025 pilot study, ten people with prediabetes had a lower glucose response while repeating the movement throughout a two-hour test involving a glucose drink test. This does not show that a few heel raises after

would have the same effect or improve glucose control over time.

Sleep matters too. Glucose regulation also depends on how effectively the body responds to

, known as insulin sensitivity.

A review combining results from randomised studies found that restricting sleep reduced insulin sensitivity in healthy adults. This supports paying attention to sleep

food and activity, although it does not show that an extra hour in bed will produce a particular glucose reading.

Put readings in context

Wearable continuous glucose monitors use a small sensor

the skin to measure glucose in the fluid between cells and estimate glucose levels. They can be valuable in diabetes care, but current diagnostic guidance says there is insufficient evidence to use them to

diabetes or prediabetes.

Diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests, usually with a second abnormal result to confirm the diagnosis

it is already clear. A standard glucose-tolerance test uses a measured glucose drink, so its diagnostic thresholds cannot simply be applied to a reading after an ordinary meal.

People with diabetes need advice tailored to their medication and

. Some treatments, including insulin, can cause dangerously low blood glucose, so lower readings are not always better.

For most people without diabetes, there is no established need to
every rise after eating. Focus instead on sustainable habits, such as including more fibre-rich foods, moving regularly and getting adequate sleep, rather than judging each meal by a glucose
. If you repeatedly see unexpected readings or have symptoms that concern you, seek medical advice.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Early biological mechanisms help babies distinguish between day and night.
Managing blood sugar requires understanding which strategies actually reduce glucose spikes.
Body weight reflects interacting biological, social and environmental influences.
The physical properties of foods explain why freezing and thawing affect their textures differently.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: A review of clinical trials found that increasing fibre improved measures of blood glucose control in people with diabetes or prediabetes; where glucose levels are above the usual range but below the threshold for diabetes.

questions.prompt: Which dietary factors influence the rise in blood glucose after a meal?
options: Neither the type nor quantity of food
Only the colour of the plate
Only the time spent reading the menu
Both the type and amount of carbohydrate eaten
questions.explanation: 第 6 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: The type and amount of carbohydrate you eat affect how much your blood glucose rises after eating.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 11?
options: The study cannot tell us exactly what a ten-minute walk will do after an ordinary meal for people of different ages and health backgrounds.
Seeing that rise on a wearable monitor can make an ordinary meal look worrying.
But a higher reading after lunch does not, by itself, mean that something has gone wrong.
However, these short studies, mainly involving young adults, do not show whether eating foods in a particular order prevents diabetes or improves long term health.
questions.explanation: 定位第 11 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
